newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-CUBS SET ALL-TIME NATIONAL LEAGUE MARK FOR WORST START.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-CUBS SET ALL-TIME NATIONAL LEAGUE MARK FOR WORST START.

text.p: Roger Bailey tossed a five-hitter for his first career shutout as the Colorado Rockies posted a 4-0 win Wednesday over the Chicago Cubs, who set the all-time National League record for worst start to a season.

Bailey (2-0), making his second start this season, threw the first complete game of his first career against the hapless Cubs, who fell to 0-12 to break the 1884 Detroit Wolverines' all-time NL record for losses to start a season.
Chicago is a loss away from matching the second-worst start in modern history, a dubious distinction shared by the 1904 Washington Senators and 1920 Detroit Tigers of the American League.
The major-league record of 0-21 was set by the American League's Baltimore Orioles in 1988.
The Cubs have an off day Thursday and then begin a six-game road trip, with four games against the New York Mets and two with the Montreal Expos.
Frank Castillo (0-3) was the loser, allowing three runs -- one earned -- and four hits with two strikeouts and two walks over 5 1/3 innings.
Since an 0-2 start, the Rockies have won 10 of 11 games, including six in a row on the road. The Rockies have won their last five games at Wrigley Field.
